newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian Telekom H1 1996 net profit jumps.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian Telekom H1 1996 net profit jumps.

text.p: Slovenian telecommunications company Telekom said on Monday its first-half net profit rose to 2.3 billion tolars ($16.7 million) from 0.5 billion in the same period of 1995.

"Our profit was up because of an eight-percent increase of prices of domestic calls in September 1995, an increased number of telephone lines and a new marketing strategy launched in April," Telekom spokesman Boris Ziherl told Reuters.
He said the firm's income in the first half of 1996 rose 26 percent to 21.4 billion tolors while the number of telephone lines increased to 637,912 by the end of June from 614,796 at the end of 1995.
Telekom, which is 74 percent owned by the Slovenian government, expects net profit to rise to 5.3 billion tolars by the end of 1995 on sales of about 43.6 billion.
